quotes.text: ChatGPT knows the public internet, but security copilot knows your environment, your sign-ins, your devices, your alerts.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Pinpoints the difference between a general AI chatbot and Security Copilot.

quotes.text: Copilot doesn't copy or store your data. It queries your systems in real time so everything stays inside your tenant.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Addresses a key data-handling concern in plain words.

quotes.text: It's not designed to replace your security team. It's designed to make your team stronger. Microsoft calls it a force multiplier, and that's exactly what it is.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Frames the realistic role of AI in small security teams.

quotes.text: If permissions are too broad, co-pilot can surface sensitive data that the person running the prompt shouldn't see. A misconfigured SharePoint folder or an overshared document becomes a problem when AI can find it instantly.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains why permission hygiene must come before enabling AI.

quotes.text: The agents recommend, suggest, and surface what needs attention, but you still make the final call. Humans approve the actions, and that's by design because you don't want an AI-making security decisions without oversight.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: States the human-in-control design principle of the security agents.

chapters.title: The agents: your AI security team

takeaways: Microsoft Security Copilot is an AI layer on top of Defender, Entra, Intune and Purview that triages alerts, summarizes incidents and recommends actions using your own tenant data.
Pre-built agents such as phishing triage and conditional access optimization do the repetitive work, while humans still approve the actions.
Microsoft 365 E5 includes a monthly allotment of Security Compute Units, but you should audit permissions and oversharing before enabling it and start with a single agent.
hook: It's two in the morning and the alerts won't stop: what if an AI assistant could triage them for you? This episode explains Microsoft Security Copilot for small IT and security teams, covering Security Compute Units, the built-in agents, licensing with E5 and the governance basics to check before you switch it on.
